events.message: Collecting evidence from the repo and deck
Found 21,872 source lines, 133 test cases and 46 commits
Read 8 docs and 3 decks, opened 2 demo pages and described 2 screenshots
Temporary problem (dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free: JSON error injected into SSE stream); trying again in 30 s
The judge is writing the council review

review.task_fit: yes: the deck and live app are explicitly built for the HubMI task for ROPS Kraków, all 46 commits fall inside the event window with none before or after, and the demo responds with HTTP 200.

scores.why: All seven modules exist in code with UI, and the mandatory matchmaking genuinely retrieves cited matches from the 115-entry ROPS catalog in D1; on the dispute over documentation language, the majority view and the Polish PDFs in the repo support B and C over A's claim of English docs. The median sides with A and C against B's 9.5 because the required numeric cost estimate is missing, the tester module drafts pilot plans without tester sign-up, rating or feedback, and admin need-trend aggregation is absent.

The build is production-minded and live: Cloudflare Workers with nine D1 migrations, Payload with role-based auth, rate limiting, idempotent submissions and CI/CD to a working demo. It loses points because the cost estimate has no numbers and there is no load or production-scale evidence.

Accessibility work is verifiable in the code, with a keyboard-operable SVG map, aria attributes, a skip link, simple Polish copy and a stated WCAG 2.1 AA target. C's 7 is too strict given that A and B both confirmed the code-level effort, but the lack of any audit or user testing keeps this below the top.

Strong materials and MVP quality: 133 tests in 43 files, a 10-slide Polish deck, a video, custom illustrations and a deployed demo. Mockups are screenshots of the built app rather than design mockups, which caps the score slightly.

strengths: All seven required modules are implemented in code with backend and UI, not mockups
Matchmaking is real: an agent with read-only tools retrieves cited matches from the 115-innovation ROPS catalog imported into D1
Production-grade engineering: live Cloudflare Worker, D1 migrations, role-based auth, rate limiting, idempotent submissions, CI/CD and 133 tests
Polish throughout the UI, deck and video, with concrete accessibility work visible in the code
weaknesses: Missing the required numeric estimate of running and maintenance costs, a submission requirement all three members confirm is unmet
Innovation tester module is reinterpreted as pilot-plan drafting with no tester sign-up, rating or feedback collection
No need-trend aggregation for administrators even though chat telemetry is stored
WCAG 2.1 AA is a stated target with no audit or user-testing evidence, and mockups are app screenshots rather than design mockups
review.verdict: An unusually complete and genuinely working build of all seven HubMI modules with real AI matchmaking over the ROPS catalog and production-grade deployment, held back by the missing numeric cost estimate, a reinterpreted tester module and unverified WCAG compliance.
